name: JNVST Class 6
fullName: Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Selection Test – Class VI
conductingBody: Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS), Ministry of Education
approxCandidates: ≈30 lakh registrations a year for about 49,000 Class 6 seats in 650+ JNVs
eligibility: Studying in Class 5 in 2026-27 in a recognised school of the same district; born 1 May 2015 – 31 Jul 2017 (for JNVST 2027); 75% seats for rural candidates; one attempt only

notification.summary: JNVST 2027 (admission session 2027-28) registration opened in early July 2026 and, after extensions, closed on 10 Aug 2026 (correction window 11–12 Aug). The test is scheduled in a single phase on Saturday, 28 Nov 2026, 11:30 AM – 1:30 PM. Admit cards are expected about 3–4 weeks before the exam and results around March 2027.

pattern.notes: Each question carries 1.25 marks and there is no negative marking. 10 extra minutes are given to read instructions. The real Mental Ability section is entirely figure-based (10 parts × 4 questions). Because this mock is text-only, the figure questions are replaced by text equivalents (letter/number patterns, described folds and mirrors, cube/dice facts) that test the same skills. The Language test uses 4 passages × 5 questions; here passages are repeated inside each question.

trendAnalysis.summary: Based on the 2024 paper and the two-phase 2025 and 2026 tests. The pattern has been fixed since 2020: Mental Ability (50%) decides the merit, with odd-one-out, figure series, mirror imaging, punched-hole and embedded-figure items of easy to moderate level. Arithmetic covers the Class 5 syllabus, with number system, fractions/decimals, measurement, percentage/profit-loss and area-perimeter being the high-yield topics; recent papers favour short word problems over plain computation. The Language test has four easy factual passages, with occasional vocabulary-in-context and title questions. Overall difficulty is easy to moderate; speed and accuracy in Mental Ability matter most.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the JNVST 2024 paper and the Phase-1/Phase-2 papers of JNVST 2025 and 2026 as reproduced in unofficial answer keys and solved-paper compilations (Careers360 answer-key pages, Arihant solved papers; found via web search, Oct 2026) and the writer's own knowledge of these papers. Official NVS papers could not be fetched. The real Mental Ability Test is figure-based (10 parts × 4); each archetype describes the figure pattern, and the mock renders it as an equivalent text item testing the same skill.

archetypes.pattern: Four of five figures share a property (category, closed/open, symmetry); pick the one that differs – text version: four items of a category with one misfit
Odd item by a number/letter property (multiples, consecutive letters, sides of shapes)
Find the exact copy of a given figure among near-identical options (one element swapped, flipped or changed)
Match a sequence of small symbols/shapes where distractors swap two adjacent elements
Complete a grid where each row follows one rule (product, sum, difference); find the missing cell
Complete a symmetric square design: given one quarter, find the missing quarter by reflection about the centre lines
Next term in a progression (elements added, ×2+1 growth, triangular numbers, letter skips)
Element rotates by a fixed angle (45°/90°) each step; predict its position after n steps
A : B :: C : ? – same relation (part–whole, number of sides, object–body part)
Analogy by transformation: letter shift, power or count change applied to the second pair
Which pieces join to make a complete square/circle/triangle; or what shapes result when a figure is cut
How many pieces/parts are needed or formed to complete a figure (counting parts of a divided shape)
Mirror image (vertical mirror) of letters, words or a clock face
Which letter/digit stays unchanged in a vertical or water (horizontal) mirror
Paper folded 1–3 times and punched; number of holes after unfolding (doubles with each fold)
Position of holes after unfolding – mirror positions across the fold line
Dice: opposite/adjacent faces using opposite-sum-7 or two views of the same die
Painted cube cut into small cubes; count cubes with 0/1/2/3 painted faces, or identify which shape/net forms a cube
Find the option in which the given small figure is hidden – text version: hidden word inside a longer word
Count the triangles/squares hidden in a composite figure
Place value/face value, expanded form, comparison of large numbers
Form the smallest/largest number from given digits; Roman numerals; even/odd and prime facts
LCM/HCF of small numbers, often as a word problem (bells, remainder, greatest length)
Add/subtract fractions in a word problem ('what fraction is left'); compare fractions
Decimal multiplication/division with place-value traps (0.01 vs 0.1)
Multi-step word problem with ×, ÷, +, − (boxes, items, money)
Percentage of a quantity or the complementary part (boys/girls, pass/fail)
Profit/loss and profit/loss per cent from CP and SP
SI, rate or time using SI = P × R × T / 100
Distance = speed × time with hours/minutes, or same speed for a new distance
Unit conversion and addition of compound units (km–m, kg–g, L–mL)
Time duration between two clock times / hours–minutes conversion
Perimeter/area of squares and rectangles, including tiles needed or equal perimeters
Volume of cube/cuboid
Angles of triangles, clock-hand turning, right/straight angles
Properties of shapes: sides, vertices, diagonals
Direct-detail question (who/what/where) answered by one sentence of a short passage
'Why' question whose answer is a stated reason in the passage; distractors are details from other sentences
Meaning of a word/phrase as used in the passage
Synonym/opposite of a word taken from the passage
Most suitable title for the passage
Inference: quality of a character, main idea or lesson of the passage

resources.notes: NVS publishes the prospectus with sample questions (linked as officialMock) for each section on navodaya.gov.in. Answer keys and question papers are not released officially; past papers circulate through publishers. Results are published district-wise on navodaya.gov.in and the CBSE ITMS portal (cbseitms.rcil.gov.in).

questions.question: Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Apple, mango and banana are fruits; potato is a vegetable (an underground stem).

questions.question: Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: 4, 8 and 12 are even numbers (and multiples of 4); 15 is odd.

questions.question: Find the odd letter-pair out.
questions.explanation: AB, CD and EF are pairs of consecutive letters; in GI the letter H is skipped.

questions.question: Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Circle, square and triangle are flat (2-D) figures; a cube is a solid (3-D) figure.

questions.question: What comes next in the series: 1, 4, 9, 16, ?
questions.explanation: These are squares: 1², 2², 3², 4², so the next term is 5² = 25.

questions.question: What comes next in the series: Z, X, V, T, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter goes two steps back in the alphabet: T − 2 = R.

questions.question: What comes next in the series: AZ, BY, CX, ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) and the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W): DW.

questions.question: A series of shapes is: triangle, square, pentagon, ? Which shape comes next?
questions.explanation: The number of sides increases by one each time: 3, 4, 5, so the next shape has 6 sides – a hexagon.

questions.question: An arrow points North. In each step of a figure series it turns 90° clockwise. In which direction does it point after 3 steps?
questions.explanation: North → East (1) → South (2) → West (3).

questions.question: What comes next in the series: 5, 10, 20, 40, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is double the previous one: 40 × 2 = 80.

questions.question: Bird : Nest :: Bee : ?
questions.explanation: A bird lives in a nest; a bee lives in a hive. A den is for a lion, a burrow for a rabbit and a stable for a horse.

questions.question: Square : 4 :: Triangle : ?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 sides; a triangle has 3 sides.

questions.question: ACE : BDF :: GIK : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter of ACE moves one step forward to make BDF. So G→H, I→J, K→L gives HJL.

questions.question: The small letter 'b' is seen in a mirror placed upright to its right. How does its mirror image look?
questions.explanation: An upright (vertical) mirror swaps left and right but keeps up and down. The bowl of 'b' moves from the right side to the left, so it looks like 'd'.

questions.question: Which of these capital letters looks exactly the same in an upright mirror placed beside it?
questions.explanation: An upright mirror reverses left and right. 'A' has a vertical line of symmetry, so it looks the same. B, E and K are symmetric only about a horizontal line, so they look reversed.

questions.question: A wall clock without numbers is seen in a mirror and appears to show 3:00. What is the actual time?
questions.explanation: For a mirror image of a clock, actual time = 12:00 − time shown = 12:00 − 3:00 = 9:00. (At 9:00 the hour hand points left; in the mirror it appears to point right, like 3:00.)

questions.question: The word TOM is written on a card and seen in an upright mirror placed beside it. Since T, O and M are each symmetric about a vertical line, what does the image read?
questions.explanation: An upright mirror reverses the order of letters; because T, O and M look the same when flipped, the image reads MOT.

questions.question: Which option is exactly the same as BD8QP6?
questions.explanation: Only BD8QP6 matches every character in the same order; the others swap P/Q, B/D or 8/6.

questions.question: Which option is exactly the same as MN5W2V?
questions.explanation: Compare character by character: only MN5W2V matches. The others swap M/N, W/V or 5/2.

questions.question: Find the missing number in this pattern. Row 1: 2, 4, 8. Row 2: 3, 6, 12. Row 3: 5, 10, ?
questions.explanation: In each row every number is double the one before it: 10 × 2 = 20.

questions.question: Find the missing number. Row 1: 3, 4, 7. Row 2: 5, 2, 7. Row 3: 6, ?, 7
questions.explanation: In each row, first number + second number = third number: 6 + 1 = 7.

questions.question: Two identical right-angled isosceles triangles are joined along their longest sides. Which figure is formed?
questions.explanation: Joining two equal isosceles right triangles along the hypotenuse gives four equal sides and four right angles – a square.

questions.question: Into how many equal parts do the two diagonals of a square divide it?
questions.explanation: The two diagonals cross at the centre and make 4 equal triangles.

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded once in half, and one hole is punched through both layers. How many holes will there be when the sheet is unfolded?
questions.explanation: The punch goes through 2 layers, so 2 holes appear, placed symmetrically about the fold line.

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded in half and then folded in half again. One hole is punched through all the layers. How many holes will there be when it is fully unfolded?
questions.explanation: Two folds make 4 layers, so one punch makes 4 holes.

questions.question: On a standard dice, the numbers on opposite faces always add up to 7. Which number is opposite the face showing 2?
questions.explanation: 2 + 5 = 7, so 5 is opposite 2.

questions.question: A wooden cube painted on all its faces is cut into 27 equal smaller cubes. How many small cubes have no paint on any face?
questions.explanation: A 3 × 3 × 3 cube has only one cube hidden in the centre: (3 − 2)³ = 1.

questions.question: Which of these words is hidden (letters together, in the same order) in the word CATERPILLAR?
questions.explanation: CATER-PILLAR contains PILLAR as a continuous part. The other words do not appear as continuous letters.

questions.question: In which of these words is the word ANT hidden (letters together, in the same order)?
questions.explanation: PL-ANT contains 'ANT'. PAINT has 'AINT', TAN has the letters in a different order, and NEAT does not contain it.

questions.question: What is the place value of 7 in 47,325?
questions.explanation: 7 is in the thousands place, so its place value is 7 × 1000 = 7,000.

questions.question: Which number does the Roman numeral XLIV stand for?
questions.explanation: XL = 40 and IV = 4, so XLIV = 44.

questions.question: What is the LCM of 4, 6 and 8?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24 … 24 is the first one divisible by both 4 and 6.

questions.question: What is the HCF of 36 and 48?
questions.explanation: 36 = 12 × 3 and 48 = 12 × 4, and 3 and 4 have no common factor, so the HCF is 12.
25 × 4 = 100; there are 3 decimal places in total, so the answer is 0.100 = 0.1.

questions.question: What is 25% of 360?
A toy bought for ₹250 is sold for ₹300. What is the profit per cent?
What is the simple interest on ₹800 at 5% per year for 3 years?
A car travels at 60 km per hour. How far will it go in 2½ hours?
questions.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

questions.question: 3 km 250 m is equal to how many metres?
How many minutes are there in 2½ hours?
questions.explanation: 2 hours = 120 minutes and ½ hour = 30 minutes; total 150 minutes.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a square of side 9 cm?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 4 × side = 4 × 9 = 36 cm.

questions.question: What is the area of a rectangular field 15 m long and 8 m wide?
questions.explanation: Area = length × breadth = 15 × 8 = 120 m².

questions.question: What is the measure of each angle of an equilateral triangle?
questions.explanation: All three angles are equal and add up to 180°, so each is 60°.

questions.question:
Passage: Sundarpur was a small village with a big pond at its centre. Every summer the pond dried up, and the women had to walk three kilometres to fetch water. One year, the school teacher, Mr. Rao, asked the children to help. Together with their parents, they cleaned the pond, removed the plastic waste and dug small channels so that rainwater from the fields would flow into it. When the monsoon came, the pond filled to the brim. By the next summer there was still water in it, and the women no longer had to walk far. The villagers decided to celebrate 'Pond Day' every year.

Question: Why did the women have to walk three kilometres in summer?
options: Because the pond was very dirty
Because they wanted to meet friends
Because the teacher told them to
questions.explanation: The passage says that every summer the pond dried up, so the women had to fetch water from three kilometres away.

questions.question:
Passage: Honeybees live together in large groups called colonies. Each colony has one queen, a few hundred drones and thousands of worker bees. The queen lays eggs, while the workers do almost all the other jobs: they build the honeycomb with wax, clean the hive, guard the entrance and collect nectar from flowers. A worker bee that finds a good patch of flowers returns to the hive and performs a 'waggle dance' to tell the others where the flowers are. As bees move from flower to flower, they carry pollen, which helps plants produce fruits and seeds.

Question: Who lays the eggs in a honeybee colony?
questions.explanation: 'The queen lays eggs, while the workers do almost all the other jobs.'

Passage: On her way to school, Meena found a purse lying near the bus stop. It contained some money and the identity card of an old man named Harish Chand. Although she was getting late, Meena went to the nearby police chowki and handed over the purse. The next day, the police officer and Mr. Harish Chand visited her school. Mr. Chand said the money was meant for his wife's medicines. The principal praised Meena in the morning assembly, and her classmates clapped loudly.

Question: Where did Meena find the purse?
questions.explanation: 'Meena found a purse lying near the bus stop.'

questions.question: Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Rose, lotus and lily are flowers; neem is a tree.

questions.question: Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: 21, 35 and 49 are multiples of 7; 54 is not.

questions.question: Find the odd letter-group out.
questions.explanation: PQR, DEF and STU are three consecutive letters; in JLM the letter K is skipped.

questions.question: Which option is exactly the same as K7RZ3M?
questions.explanation: Only K7RZ3M matches every character in order; the others swap R/Z or change 7→1 or 3→8.

questions.question: Which option is exactly the same as ▲●■◆?
questions.explanation: The distractors each swap two neighbouring symbols; only ▲●■◆ keeps the original order.

questions.question: Which option is exactly the same as pqbd96?
questions.explanation: Mirror-type letters (p/q, b/d) and digits (6/9) are swapped in the distractors; only pqbd96 is identical.

questions.question: Find the missing number. Row 1: 4, 5, 20. Row 2: 3, 6, 18. Row 3: 7, 2, ?
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the product of the first two: 4 × 5 = 20, 3 × 6 = 18, so 7 × 2 = 14.

questions.question: Find the missing number. Row 1: 10, 4, 6. Row 2: 15, 7, 8. Row 3: 20, 9, ?
questions.explanation: In each row the third number = first − second: 10 − 4 = 6, 15 − 7 = 8, so 20 − 9 = 11.

questions.question: A square design is divided into four equal quarters. The top-left quarter shows an arrow ↖ pointing to its outer corner. The design is symmetric about both its vertical and horizontal centre lines. What does the bottom-right quarter show?
questions.explanation: Reflecting ↖ about the vertical line gives ↗ in the top-right quarter; reflecting that about the horizontal line gives ↘ in the bottom-right quarter.

questions.question: What comes next in the series: 2, 5, 11, 23, ?
questions.explanation: Each term = previous term × 2 + 1: 23 × 2 + 1 = 47.

questions.question: In a figure series, a clock hand starts pointing at 12 and turns 45° anticlockwise at every step. At which number does it point after 4 steps?
questions.explanation: 4 × 45° = 180°. Turning half a circle from 12 (in either direction) brings the hand to 6.

questions.question: Dots are arranged in triangles: the 1st figure has 1 dot, the 2nd has 3, the 3rd has 6 and the 4th has 10. How many dots will the 5th figure have?
questions.explanation: Each new row adds one more dot than the last: +2, +3, +4, so the next step is +5: 10 + 5 = 15.

questions.question: Fish : Fins :: Bird : ?
questions.explanation: A fish moves with its fins; a bird moves with its wings.

questions.question: Pentagon : 5 :: Hexagon : ?
questions.explanation: A pentagon has 5 sides; a hexagon has 6 sides.

questions.question: AB : DE :: PQ : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves three places forward: A→D, B→E; so P→S, Q→T, giving ST.

questions.question: Which pair of pieces can be joined to make one complete circle?
questions.explanation: Two halves make a whole: two semicircles form a full circle. The other pairs cover only ½, ¾ or ¾ of a circle.

questions.question: A rectangle is cut along one of its diagonals. Which shapes are the two pieces?
questions.explanation: A diagonal joins opposite corners, so each piece keeps one 90° corner of the rectangle: two right-angled triangles.

questions.question: Three identical small squares are placed side by side in a row. How many more such squares are needed to make one big square of 3 × 3?
questions.explanation: A 3 × 3 square needs 9 small squares; 9 − 3 = 6 more are needed.

questions.question: The word MAT is written on a card and seen in an upright mirror placed beside it. Since M, A and T each look the same in such a mirror, what does the image read?
questions.explanation: A side mirror reverses left and right, so the letter order is reversed; each letter is unchanged, giving TAM.

questions.question: A wall clock without numbers, seen in a mirror, appears to show 4:00. What is the actual time?
questions.explanation: For whole hours, actual time = 12:00 − mirror time = 12:00 − 4:00 = 8:00.

questions.question: Which of these digits looks exactly the same when its image is seen in water (a mirror placed below it)?
questions.explanation: A water image flips top and bottom. The digit 3 is symmetric about a horizontal line, so it looks the same; 4, 7 and 6 change.

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded in half three times, one fold after another. One hole is then punched through all the layers. How many holes will there be when the sheet is fully unfolded?
questions.explanation: Each fold doubles the layers: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 layers, so one punch makes 8 holes.

questions.question: A sheet of paper is folded along its vertical middle line so that the left half lies exactly on the right half. One hole is punched in the upper part of the folded sheet. Where will the holes be after unfolding?
options: Only one hole, in the upper right
One hole in the upper half and one in the lower half
Two holes, both on the right half
Two holes in the upper half, one on each side of the fold line
questions.explanation: The punch passes through both halves, so the holes appear at mirror positions on either side of the vertical fold, both in the upper half.

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded once along a diagonal to make a triangle. Two holes are punched through the folded sheet. How many holes will there be when it is unfolded?
questions.explanation: One fold makes two layers, so each of the 2 punches makes 2 holes: 2 × 2 = 4.

questions.question: On a standard dice the numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. Which pair of numbers can never be seen on adjacent (touching) faces?
questions.explanation: 3 + 4 = 7, so 3 and 4 are on opposite faces and can never touch. The other pairs do not add to 7.

questions.question: A wooden cube painted on all faces is cut into 27 equal smaller cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
questions.explanation: Cubes with two painted faces lie on the edges but not at corners: 12 edges × 1 = 12. (8 are corners, 6 face-centres, 1 hidden.)

questions.question: A cube painted red on all faces is cut into 8 equal smaller cubes. How many small cubes have exactly three faces painted?
questions.explanation: Cutting into 2 × 2 × 2 makes every small cube a corner cube, so all 8 have three painted faces.

questions.question: Which of these words is hidden (letters together, in the same order) in the word TEMPERATURE?
questions.explanation: TEMPE-RAT-URE contains R, A, T together. The letters of PUT, MAP and TAP do not appear together in that order.

questions.question: A square has both of its diagonals drawn. How many triangles are there in the figure in all?
questions.explanation: The diagonals make 4 small triangles, and each pair of neighbouring small triangles forms a bigger triangle (4 more): 4 + 4 = 8.

questions.question: In which of these words is the word CAR hidden (letters together, in the same order)?
questions.explanation: S-CAR-F contains C, A, R together in order; the other words have these letters in a different order.

questions.question: What is the smallest 5-digit number that can be formed using the digits 4, 0, 7, 2 and 9, each used only once?
questions.explanation: 0 cannot be the first digit, so start with the next smallest, 2, then write the rest in increasing order: 20479.

questions.question: What is the difference between the place value and the face value of 6 in 56,812?
questions.explanation: Place value of 6 = 6,000; face value = 6. Difference = 6,000 − 6 = 5,994.

questions.question: What is the smallest number which, when divided by 6, 8 and 12, leaves a remainder of 3 in each case?
questions.explanation: LCM of 6, 8, 12 = 24; required number = 24 + 3 = 27.

questions.question: Riya ate 2/5 of a cake and Mohan ate 1/4 of it. What fraction of the cake is left?
A school bought 24 boxes of chalk with 36 chalks in each box. If 150 chalks have been used, how many are left?
In a class of 40 students, 35% are girls. How many boys are there in the class?
A shopkeeper buys a bag for ₹480 and sells it at a loss of ₹60. What is his loss per cent?
At what rate per cent per year will ₹600 earn a simple interest of ₹90 in 3 years?
A cyclist covers 36 km in 3 hours. At the same speed, how long will he take to cover 60 km?
questions.explanation: Speed = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 km/h. Time = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 hours.

questions.question: A train leaves a station at 10:45 a.m. and reaches its destination at 3:20 p.m. the same day. How long is the journey?
questions.explanation: 10:45 a.m. to 2:45 p.m. is 4 h; 2:45 p.m. to 3:20 p.m. is 35 min. Total 4 h 35 min.

questions.question: A room is 6 m long and 4 m wide. How many square tiles of side 50 cm are needed to cover its floor?
questions.explanation: Floor = 600 cm × 400 cm. Tiles along length = 12, along width = 8; 12 × 8 = 96.

questions.question: The perimeter of a square is equal to the perimeter of a rectangle 14 cm long and 10 cm wide. What is the side of the square?
questions.explanation: Perimeter of rectangle = 2 × (14 + 10) = 48 cm; side of square = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm.

questions.question: Through how many degrees does the minute hand of a clock turn in 20 minutes?
questions.explanation: The minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, i.e. 6° per minute: 20 × 6° = 120°.

Passage: Arjun lived in a village at the edge of a forest. Every morning he took his family's goats to graze on the hillside. One hot afternoon he noticed smoke rising from the dry grass near the forest. He knew that even a small fire could spread quickly in the strong summer wind. Arjun ran to the nearest house, which had a mobile phone, and called the forest office. Then he alerted the villagers, who carried buckets of water and beat the flames with green branches. By the time the forest guards arrived, the fire was almost out. The forest officer thanked Arjun and gave him a book about the birds and animals of the forest.

Question: What did Arjun do every morning?
options: He collected dry grass for the fire
He went to school in the town
He worked at the forest office
He took the goats to graze on the hillside
questions.explanation: The passage says that every morning he took his family's goats to graze on the hillside.

questions.question:
Passage: The camel is well suited to life in the desert. Its long legs keep its body away from the hot sand, and its broad, padded feet do not sink into it. Long eyelashes and nostrils that can close protect it from blowing sand. Many people believe that a camel stores water in its hump, but this is not true. The hump is a store of fat, which the animal uses for energy when food is scarce. A thirsty camel can drink a very large amount of water in a few minutes. Because it can carry heavy loads across long distances of sand, the camel is often called the 'ship of the desert'.

Question: What does a camel store in its hump?
questions.explanation: The passage says the hump is a store of fat, not water.

Passage: Paper is made from wood pulp, so every sheet we waste means that more trees have to be cut. Old newspapers, notebooks and cartons can be recycled. At a recycling unit, used paper is first soaked in water and beaten into a soft pulp. The ink is washed away, and the clean pulp is pressed and dried into new sheets. Making paper in this way uses less water and energy than making it from fresh wood. Students can help by writing on both sides of a page, using old calendars as book covers and keeping waste paper separate from wet kitchen waste.

Question: What is paper made from, according to the passage?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says paper is made from wood pulp.
